### Summary

This section keeps the selector of the fourth-order reference and its guards; the construction itself, the
four-cell face rule, is derived in @sec-ch05-wbref4 and is not repeated here.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Selects the reference face rule of @sec-ch05-wbref4.

**Data.** The kernel's cell density reference and scan pressures in; the face density reference out.

**Placement.** Before the well-balanced radial perturbation reconstruction.

**Activation.** `SNAP_WB_REF4=1`, default off; XC also enables it.

**Guarantee / limits.** Cubic exactness on uniform grids; unusable stencils keep the base reference.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-wb-reference-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

Local symbols: $\rho$[^rg-afba7fb0b9e7] is density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], $p$[^rg-f3f9358ec424] pressure [Pa], and $\chi=\rho/p$
[$\mathrm{s^2\,m^{-2}}$].

### Derivation

See @sec-ch05-wbref4 for the face rule and its guards. The chapter's own check line `[C2]` re-derives the
face rule independently: it integrates the quartic interpolant exactly [check
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`]. The same line also verifies a five-point filter and a
cubic wall continuation, which no operator of the switch uses.

### Numerical method

The switch is read once per process by `wb_ref4_enabled` ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}),
which also returns true when `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` does. With nonzero $g_1$[^rg-a803b0bc6ed1] the setup of the hydro
module refuses fewer than three ghost cells (`HydroImpl::reset`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}),
because the resolution flag reads pressures three cells away; with zero gravity no reference is built and the
guard is inactive. `wb_ref4_stencils` ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}}) builds the stencils
once per grid and marks them usable only with at least five cells and, next to a clamped wall, at least four
owned cells; a block between two seams reads its exchanged ghosts instead. `wb_ref4_flag`
({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}}) builds the resolution flag and dilates it by two cells, and
`wb_ref4_faces` ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}}) applies the face rule after the seam
exchange of the cell reference, keeping the base face value where the stencil is unusable, where the flag is set
or where the new value leaves the range of its two cells. The cell reference is not touched. Both run inside `HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}})
with the wall-clamp flags of @sec-ch11-wb.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch12-wb-reference-flow
#| fig-cap: "The four-cell face window of the reference: sky-blue circles are the kernel's cell density references, black ticks are faces, and the labels give the face weights."
#| fig-alt: "four cells and five faces with the weights of the interior and wall face rows."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch12.figures.fig_wb_reference_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

**How to use it.** Set `SNAP_WB_REF4=1` before launch and merge this fragment into a complete input card.
Use `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=0` when isolating WB from XC:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `geometry`[^rg-d507df17a90e], `cells`[^rg-3ae5045adadc], `nghost`[^rg-2629ff7b5445], `forcing`[^rg-a13a781de491], `const-gravity`[^rg-138bbf245f63], `grav1`[^rg-96f8ca6235cd], `gravity-work`[^rg-334e37910182].
```yaml
geometry:
  cells:
    nghost: 3
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8     # m s^-2
    gravity-work: cell
```

With radial gravity, `HydroImpl::reset` refuses a thinner halo: for two ghosts the message is
"SNAP_WB_REF4 (or SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT, which implies it, or dynamics/conversion-order 4) needs nghost >= 3,
got 2".
The pressure scan needs those three neighbours; zero gravity disables that guard.

`wb_ref4_enabled` ({{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}) contains this selection step:

```cpp
  return on || x1_centroid_exact_enabled();
```

The logical OR selects the reference whenever either switch is active. It chooses the face rule checked by
`[C2]`; it does not remove its stencil-usability fallback.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| flag | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}} | `wb_ref4_enabled` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |
| guard | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `nghost` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |
| stencils | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_stencils >}} | `usable` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |
| flag | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_flag >}} | `wb_ref4_flag` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |
| faces | {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_faces >}} | `wb_ref4_faces` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |
| call | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}} | `wb_ref4` | `SNAP_WB_REF4` |

: Implementation sites for the fourth-order reference selector. {#tbl-ch12-wb-reference-code}

1. Read the switch once, or inherit it from XC. The anchor `wb_ref4_enabled` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}.
2. At setup with gravity, refuse fewer than three ghosts. The anchor `nghost` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}.
3. On each hydro call build or reuse the stencils, build the resolution flag, exchange the seam rows, apply the
   face rule. The anchor `wb_ref4` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_wb_ref4_order_python` (CUDA variant registered) | three-resolution order of the spurious stratification, on and off arms, FC on in both | on: slope at least 2.75; off: below 2.5 | `ORDER_ON`, `ORDER_OFF` |
| `test_x1_seam_split_wb_ref4.<b>` (CUDA and two-rank variants registered) | a split column matches one block; `nghost` below 3 is refused | relative gap at most $10^{-13}$; exception text | the test |
| `test_x1_seam_split_wb_ref4_gravity_0.<b>` | with zero gravity a one-ghost column sets up and steps | finite state | the test |
| `test_balance_column_wb_ref4.<b>`, `test_face_floor_wb_ref4.<b>` | the balance and face-floor checks hold under the switched reference | as in their base tests | `tests/CMakeLists.txt` |
| `configuration_check.py` `[C2]` (report check) | the face moments | exact symbolic or Boolean equality | the independent check |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-wb-reference-tests}

The thresholds are `ORDER_ON` and `ORDER_OFF` ({{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py ORDER_ON >}},
{{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py ORDER_OFF >}}), applied in `main`
({{< code tests/test_wb_ref4_order.py main >}}); the seam assertions are
{{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.wb_ref4_flag_at_the_seam_split_matches_one_block >}} and
{{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.wb_ref4_gravity_0_nghost_1_steps >}}; the switched arms are
registered in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}.

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch15-ch12-tests.

The independent report check verifies the face moments in `[C2]`.[^ch12-wb-reference-run] The check itself is
unchanged, so its committed output line still reads `filter, cubic wall continuation and face moments`; those
two identities belong to an operator the switch no longer has, and no claim here rests on them.
It models the stated contract; it does not execute the compiled solver.

[^ch12-wb-reference-run]: [sha: snapy@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f; deck: the check itself;
    run: `python src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, CPU, one process;
    Python 3.12.10, numpy 2.5.4, sympy 1.14.0]. Exact symbolic and Boolean assertions; no floating-point tolerance.
    Output `configuration_check.out`, `[C2]`; reproduced for this edit. Solver CTests are source-inspected only.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
No fitted order is measured here. The guards can lower the effective order near walls and seams, and the
interior moments say nothing about wall or gnomonic convergence. Gnomonic grids and the wider switch combinations
are gaps in @sec-ch12-matrix.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::

[^rg-96f8ca6235cd]: grav1 — gravity component along the first coordinate

[^rg-334e37910182]: gravity-work — form of the $x_1$ gravity work: `face` (default), `face-wallc` or `cell`
